children: Singapore's central bank is likely to tighten its monetary-policy settings at its meeting due Wednesday, according to 10 of 11 economists polled by the Wall Street Journal. Moody's Analytics expects the Monetary Authority of Singapore to tighten policy by raising the rate of appreciation of the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate policy band, citing likely elevated energy and food prices. "Singapore is highly import-dependent, and the pass-through of global prices into consumer prices is relatively fast," says Denise Cheok, head of Southeast Asia economics, in an email. "Robust export demand gives MAS room to tighten further to fend off imported inflation." The MAS uses the exchange rate as a policy tool for maintaining price stability, given Singapore's small and open economy. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
